blocks.h2: How a Tankless Water Heater Works
blocks.body: A tankless water heater heats water only when you open a hot tap. Water runs through a heat exchanger, a gas burner or electric element heats it on the spot, and it flows to the fixture. There's no tank to keep hot around the clock, so you don't run out halfway through a shower. The tradeoff is that the unit has to be sized for how much hot water you use at the same time, and it needs the gas supply, venting or electrical service to match.

blocks.h2: Tankless in Older Highland Park Homes
blocks.intro: Nearly half of Highland Park homes were built before 1960. Tankless can be a great upgrade, but older homes need a closer look first.

items.body: A gas tankless unit often needs more gas than the old tank did. In older homes, that can mean upsizing the line. See [gas line installation](/highland-park/gas-line-installation).
Tankless units vent differently from tank heaters, and electric models can need a panel upgrade. We check both before we quote, so you don't find out halfway through the job.
In a Lake County winter, incoming water is much colder, so the unit has to heat it further. We size tankless units for winter, when they have to work hardest.

blocks.h2: Tankless Water Heater Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: Is a tankless water heater worth it?
items.preview: Often, yes. But older homes may need gas, venting or electrical upgrades first.
items.answer: For many homes, yes: continuous hot water, less space and often a longer life. But the install can cost more when an older home needs a larger gas line, new venting or electrical work. We'll show you what your home needs so you can decide.

items.q: Can my older home support a tankless water heater?
items.preview: Most can. We check gas capacity, venting and electrical before quoting.
items.answer: Most can, with the right upgrades. The questions are gas line capacity, venting and, for electric units, your electrical panel. We check all three before quoting.

items.q: Do you repair tankless water heaters?
items.preview: Yes. Scale, ignition and error codes are the most common issues.
items.answer: Yes. Common problems include scale buildup, ignition or flame sensor issues, error codes and venting problems. Regular descaling prevents many of them.

items.q: How much does a tankless water heater cost to install?
items.preview: It depends on the unit and any upgrades. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the unit, whether you need gas, venting or electrical upgrades, and where it's mounted. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins, and financing is available.
